Guerlain revisits an icon: L'Heure Bleue

Guerlain revisits one of the most storied creations in its perfume organ: L'Heure Bleue, composed more than a century ago and still considered a landmark of modern perfumery for its trail of carnation, violet, and vanilla.

The Maison introduces a new extrait expression that concentrates the original accord while adding facets of iris and white musk, presented in the historic quadrilobe bottle blown to the original specifications.

Master perfumers describe the exercise as restoration rather than reinvention: gas-chromatography archives of early batches guided the reconstruction of top notes that had drifted with changes in raw-material regulations.

The launch is supported by an exhibition at the Maison's Paris address tracing a century of the scent through advertising posters, flacons, and client correspondence.
